summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): İstanbul — the whole scene; the Beyoğlu legacy: the district governor's office ordered trans women's apartments on Bayram Street sealed in March 2024; on 18 July 2025 a residential street was blockaded by police with drones and raids (three detained); on 31 July 2025 around 20 trans women were rounded up for identity checks while street, shopping and in cafés, taken to a police station, names recorded and videos filmed ('this is profiling'). Pride has been banned for a ninth consecutive year — 113 detained on 25 June 2023, 46 detained at the 2024 Acıbadem march with judicial controls and travel bans. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey.

sources.summary: Human Rights Watch (29 Oct 2025): a leaked '11th Judicial Package' would amend the penal and civil codes with articles threatening LGBT people — behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' and its 'promotion' (up to three years' prison, amending the indecent-acts provision); sharp restrictions on gender-affirming care (minimum age 25, onerous eligibility); potential charges against trans people, care providers, civil-society organisations and journalists; justified as protecting 'the family and public morals'.

Kaos GL's LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025, 'The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People': hostility institutionalised as explicit state policy — presidency-centred targeting, the family ministry as implementing body, religious-broadcast regulator and content restrictions on expression and artistic freedom, one LGBTI+ organisation closed, digital-platform penalties and broadcast censorship; six violations of the right to life documented (three recorded as hate-motivated), trans people the most affected; no state hate-crime statistics exist so data rests on media reporting. Launched at a public event in the capital.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (nav-only cache); the underlying news report covers the 31 July 2025 roundup of around 20 trans women in this city's Beyoğlu district for ID checks — names recorded, videos taken, 'this is profiling'.

tangentialFactors: State penalties on LGBT-inclusive digital content and broadcasts (censorship, platform fines, broadcaster withdrawals) plus blanket event bans form a national hostility climate implemented locally, affecting queer visibility broadly rather than gender identity per se.
localsOnly: The draft law package's gender-affirming care restrictions (minimum age 25, eligibility conditions) and national health-ministry trans-care rules bear on residents; visitors cannot obtain transition care here. Residents involved in Pride-related protests here have additionally faced judicial controls and travel bans.
